terms.gloss: you brazen face! the cheek of it!
terms.comment: Traupman’s word for “big-mouth!”, but in Latin it is cheek rather than talk: ōs, the face, is impudence, and dūrum, hard, unblushing (so ōs dūrissimum, a very brazen man, Cic. Quinct. 77).

evidence: Cic. Sen. 55: senectūs est nātūrā loquācior (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: have a sharp tongue, be a big mouth
evidence: Petr. 43.3: dūrae buccae fuit, linguōsus (Lewis & Short s.v. bucca)
terms.comment: A genitive of quality: “he was of a hard cheek”.
Lewis & Short: of a noisy speaker in oratory.

sources: Lewis & Short: os · Lewis & Short: durus · Lewis & Short: loquax · Lewis & Short: bucca
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 94, checked against the searchable text and the page images of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
